statement: Let τ(n) be the number of positive divisors of n and σ(n) be their sum. The function sum_four_divisors(nums) returns a result r and r = Σ_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} c(nums[i]), where c(n) = σ(n) if τ(n) = 4 and c(n) = 0 otherwise. The sum is over all indices, so equal values at different positions are counted separately.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10000 and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.

statement: The function sum_four_divisors(nums) returns a result (it does not fail, overflow, or panic).
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10000 and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.

statement: Whenever sum_four_divisors(nums) returns r, we have 0 ≤ r.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10000 and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.

statement: Whenever sum_four_divisors(nums) returns r, r = 0 if and only if for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), nums[i] has a number of positive divisors different from 4.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10000 and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.

statement: Whenever sum_four_divisors(nums) returns r, for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums) such that nums[i] has exactly four positive divisors, σ(nums[i]) ≤ r, where σ(n) is the sum of the positive divisors of n.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10000 and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.

statement: Whenever sum_four_divisors(nums) returns r, then for every slice nums' with the same length and the same multiset of entries as nums, every result r' returned by sum_four_divisors(nums') satisfies r' = r.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10000 and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.

statement: Fix an index i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums) such that nums[i] does not have exactly four positive divisors. Let nums' be any slice satisfying the same preconditions with len(nums') = len(nums), nums'[j] = nums[j] for every j ≠ i, and nums'[i] also not having exactly four positive divisors. Whenever sum_four_divisors(nums) returns r and sum_four_divisors(nums') returns r', we have r' = r.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10000 and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.

statement: Fix an index i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums) such that nums[i] has exactly four positive divisors. Let nums' be any slice satisfying the same preconditions with len(nums') = len(nums), nums'[j] = nums[j] for every j ≠ i, and nums'[i] having exactly four positive divisors and the same divisor sum σ(nums'[i]) = σ(nums[i]). Whenever sum_four_divisors(nums) returns r and sum_four_divisors(nums') returns r', we have r' = r.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10000 and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.

statement: Whenever sum_four_divisors(nums) returns r, let V be the set of distinct values appearing in nums, and for each v in V let k_v be the number of indices i with nums[i] = v. Then r = Σ_{v in V} (if τ(v) = 4 then k_v · σ(v) else 0), where τ(v) is the number of positive divisors of v and σ(v) is their sum.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10000 and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.

statement: Whenever sum_four_divisors(a) returns r_a, sum_four_divisors(b) returns r_b, and sum_four_divisors(nums) returns r, we have r = r_a + r_b.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10000 and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000. Let a and b be nonempty slices with nums = a ++ b.

statement: Whenever sum_four_divisors(nums) returns r, we have r ≤ 2000020000.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10000 and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000.
